text:
maya: FYI I ran the long-context repro across the multi-tenant cluster this morning. seeing steady KV mem growth on a subset of tenants, plus spikes in pagewalks.
alex: can you paste the top-level numbers? p99s, eviction rates, fragmentation metric?
maya: quick summary: for tenants T1/T2/T3 over 6h: p50 mem usage +12% (T1), +3% (T2), +40% (T3). eviction_rate avg=0.17, p95=0.31. fragmentation score ~= 23% on affected backends. pagewalks spiked ~3.5x during longctx workloads.
raj: wow T3 is the noisy neighbor. was that single-session longctx or many parallel users?
maya: multi-session longctx; we have many overlapping >16k token sessions. KV residency for T3 steadily climbed - their prefix reuse is low so we get lots of cold inserts and near-immediate evictions.
irene: did the kernel selection change recently? that could alter memory footprints or eviction cadence.
maya: no kernel rollouts last 24h. but batching heuristics did change (small tweak to merge window). tried reverting that in a canary and T3 behavior didn't improve.
alex: do we have a stack profile or flamegraph for the pagewalks? could be fragmentation forcing extra walking logic.
maya: uploaded flame snippet to S3: s3://redwood-debug/kv-longctx-flames/1799994321.png
maya: gist of the profile: heavy time in page_map_lookup and free_list_coalesce. coalescing is expensive when pages are scattered.
raj: sounds like fragmentation + high churn. any evidence of ghost pages (pages kept resident but unreachable because of metadata bug)?
maya: I grepped GC logs; there are ~120k pages marked free but not returned to host allocator for T3. suspiciously parallel to a retry path in eviction that can skip reclaim under race.
opsbot: deploybot: rolling canary started for kv-evict-fixes on cluster kv-pool-7 (build 2026.03.15-evictfix)
irene: if there's a race in eviction, per-tenant quotas will be bypassed and noisy tenant can hoard KV residency. we should short-circuit and enforce a hard soft-watermark for tenant residency until we fix.
alex: proposal: implement a tenant_soft_watermark that triggers accelerated reclaim for that tenant (aggressive compaction + deny_growth flag). start with threshold 70% of tenant quota for 2m windows.
raj: also add a smoothing function: when a tenant hits soft watermark, we do proportional throttle of new KV allocations based on moving avg of their insert rate. that avoids immediate hard cuts.
maya: rough CLI for debug I used:
```
# show per-tenant residency + fragmentation
rbin kv-inspect --pool kv-pool-7 --tenant T3 --json | jq '.residency, .frag_score, .evict_rate'
```
maya: output snippet: ["residency": 72.4MB, "frag_score": 0.23, "evict_rate": 0.31]
alex: ok. can we simulate the soft_watermark logic in the staging harness? we need to ensure latency SLOs don't tank when reclaim runs.
irene: yes. setup: staging with 3 tenants, one synthetic noisy longctx generator. run for 2h and sweep metrics: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, eviction CPU overhead.
raj: also capture resident page count over time + coalesce runtime to verify compaction cost. add tracepoint around free_list_coalesce.
maya: I'll spin a job tonight and share results in morning. if the race is real we should gate next evict change behind the short-circuit policy.
opsbot: alert: kv-pool-7 canary: build 2026.03.15-evictfix completed. 2 nodes failed healthcheck and rolled back.
maya: thanks. I'll check the rollback logs and correlate with the page counts.
alex: long-term we should add tenant-level reclamation credits that regenerate slowly and can be spent for burst longctx. gives fairness without hard stops.
irene: agree. for short term: implement tenant_soft_watermark + proportional throttle + extra observability (tracepoints, per-tenant free-list stats). prioritize a hotfix for the eviction race.
maya: adding tasks to infra board now. tagging @alex @raj for review of the canary plan. :thumbsup:
